answer.answer: The Scheme for Prevention of Alcoholism and Substance Abuse is a government initiative that provides financial assistance to support NGOs to offer treatment of addiction [E01]. The scheme was initiated in 1987 and revised as of October 1, 2008 [E01]. Its aims and objectives are to support activities of non-governmental organisations working in the areas of prevention of addiction and rehabilitation of drug users with a rights-based approach, and to create awareness about the ill-effects of substance abuse [E01]. The scheme addresses addiction in its totality, including prevention efforts, creating awareness, early identification, treatment and rehabilitation, sustained follow-up care, and community involvement [E01]. The scheme includes components such as Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts (IRCA), workplace prevention programmes, awareness-cum-de-addiction camps, and Regional Resource and Training Centres [E03].
